rationale: IT admins at SMBs running Cisco ASA/FTD are a real, paying segment — Duo and Okta prove willingness to spend on exactly this. However, a RADIUS-based MFA service requires real infrastructure (a server that handles authentication requests 24/7), compliance considerations, and per-customer configuration that Claude + a simple page cannot deliver autonomously; every deployment needs hands-on setup and ongoing uptime guarantees that a solo non-technical operator cannot sustain. Both buildability_with_ai (3) and operational_autonomy (3) badly fail their build gates, and the weighted total (4.9) falls below the 5.5 validate threshold, so this is a drop.
solution_plan: Not viable as a factory micro-service. A RADIUS MFA service is fundamentally a 24/7 infrastructure product requiring server upkeep, network-level integration, and per-customer firewall/ASA configuration — none of which Claude or a simple web page can handle autonomously. A solo non-technical operator could not realistically build or maintain this without a dedicated engineering team and security compliance posture. The idea should be dropped or re-scoped as a paid consulting referral to existing vendors.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (3 < 6) and operational_autonomy (3 < 7) build gates. Total also below validate threshold.
